hints.title: Divisor Multiplicity Principle
hints.text: A positive integer has an odd number of divisors if and only if it is a perfect square.

hints.title: Square of a Prime
hints.text: For a number to have exactly three divisors (1, p, and p^2), it must be the square of a prime number.

hints.title: Primality of the Square Root
hints.text: Check if the integer square root squared equals n, and confirm that the root itself is a prime integer.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Square root verification and primality trial division.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Looping up to n takes O(n) operations, which is slower than testing primality of root.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Checking up to fourth root of n confirms primality in constant time operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that only squares of prime numbers have exactly 3 divisors.
